UE 5.6 alpha.9 — official application marks in the transfer UI

ForgeMCP now uses the application marks directly on their corresponding connection and transfer actions. The assets are embedded in the local React bundle, so the editor tab makes no web requests to display them.

Asset provenance

  • web-ui/src/assets/partner-logos/unreal-engine.svg is copied unchanged from the UE 5.6 installation's Engine/Content/Editor/Slate/About/UnrealLogo.svg. Epic's current brand guidance is available on the Unreal Engine branding page ↗.
  • web-ui/src/assets/partner-logos/blender.svg is the Blender application mark copied unchanged from Blender's official source repository at release/freedesktop/icons/scalable/apps/blender.svg ↗. Blender's logo page ↗ describes use of its logo and brand guidelines.

The Unreal mark is used in its supplied white-on-transparent treatment; the Blender mark keeps its supplied orange, blue, and white colors. The React UI does not recolor, crop, or redraw either logo. ForgeMCP remains identified as an independent integration in the panel footer.

Placement and validation

  • Blender mark: Blender Connection heading and Send to Blender action.
  • Unreal Engine mark: Transfer to Unreal heading and Send to Unreal action.
  • Both SVGs are inlined into the single-file HTML bundle; CSP remains local-only.
  • The Unreal package verifier checked the bundled page and passed a clean UE 5.6.1 editor load, plugin health, and live MCP project identity verification.
  • The layout refinement is recorded in the compact reference-matched layout note.
  • Chromium headless rendered the updated panel with both supplied marks visible.
  • Installed UI SHA-256: 64116ca7d26460ccdb8ea8d93f4c488d28ef16ca5e1ccd57b5d250c8b2929079.
  • Alpha archive SHA-256:

The desktop Unreal WebBrowser panel still needs a visible refresh after the UI bundle update. Close and reopen the ForgeMCP tab to load the latest local page.
